elements_not_encoded.text: If short of breath or oxygen saturation < 95%, give oxygen: 1-4L/min via nasal prongs or 6-10L/min via facemask, up to 10-15L/min via non-rebreather mask. Aim f
If tension pneumothorax likely: insert large bore cannula2 above 6th rib, anterior axillary line. Arrange urgent chest tube.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Needle decompression for tension pneumothorax; management only.

elements_not_encoded.text: If shock/systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
elements_not_encoded.reason: IV fluids for shock; management only.

elements_not_encoded.text: If severe pneumonia (2 or more of: confusion/decreased level of consciousness, BP < 90/60, RR ≥ 30 or age > 65): give ceftriaxone3 1g IV/IM.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Ceftriaxone for severe pneumonia. The "2 or more of" definition only selects a treatment; no separate diagnosis or priority is stated, and "age > 65" has no form in the language.

elements_not_encoded.text: If rapid deep breathing, check fingerprick glucose. If > 11.1 19.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Glucose check pointer for rapid deep breathing; routine vital, management/cross-reference to 19.

judgment_calls.decision: AND of sudden-onset dyspnoea, (hyperresonance or decreased breath sounds or unilateral chest pain), trachea displaced, and BP < 90/60; the urgent rule uses (active_condition Tension pneumothorax)
judgment_calls.alternatives: Sudden breathlessness plus ANY of the signs; or each sign alone as an urgent item
